title: Steve Prefontaine: Munich 5000
description: A last-mile surge, a Finnish kick, and fourth place by a stride—Go Deep into Pre's Olympic heartbreak.
imageHint: A historic track under lights—legend still in the air

questions.question: In the 1972 Munich Olympic 5000m final, which American front-runner led late, then finished fourth?
questions.explanation: He took the lead with about four laps left and forced a hard pace—exactly the race he wanted. The kick at the end still wasn't enough.

questions.question: Who beat Prefontaine for gold in that Munich 5000m—days after falling in the 10,000m, then getting up to win?
questions.explanation: The Finn completed the 5k/10k double. In the 5000 he closed the last lap in about 56 seconds. Pre had no answer.

questions.question: Virén took gold; which Brit outsprinted a fading Prefontaine in the last 15 meters for bronze?
questions.explanation: Tunisia's Mohamed Gammoudi took silver. Stewart's late charge stole Pre's medal by 0.36 seconds—13:27.6 to 13:28.25.

questions.question: Before Munich and that Stewart bronze dash, Prefontaine ran collegiately for which Eugene university under Bill Bowerman?
questions.explanation: Seven NCAA titles. Hayward Field was his concert hall. Bowerman's waffle-iron experiments with Phil Knight were already becoming Nike.

questions.question: Three years after his Oregon peak and Munich heartbreak, Prefontaine died when his gold British roadster flipped on Skyline Boulevard—what model?
questions.explanation: May 30, 1975. He was 24. Runners still leave bibs and medals at the crash site—Pre's Rock—and the Prefontaine Classic still brings the world to Hayward.

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: After Munich
deeperMode.description: The first star stipend and the crash-site shrine

questions.question: In 1973 Prefontaine received a $5,000 stipend as the first star endorsement for which shoe company?
questions.hint: Bowerman and Knight's company, once Blue Ribbon Sports

questions.question: What shrine name do runners give the Skyline Boulevard crash site where they leave bibs and medals?
questions.hint: Still visited before every Prefontaine Classic

easterEgg.title: Sacrifice the gift
easterEgg.text: Biographer Tom Jordan says Pre closed talks to young athletes with: "To give anything less than your best is to sacrifice the gift." Nike's Hollister recalled hearing him say it at West Albany High. No tape of it exists.
